property_summary: Deposits with msg.value below MinDeposit do not increase the contract's ether balance.
If amount is strictly less than MinDeposit, the contract balance must not increase

Invariant: after any sequence where an account deposits some amount and then calls CashOut(x) for x <= its balance, the contract's balances mapping for that account equals its previous balance minus x (i.e., balances decrease by exactly the cashed-out amount); the mutant that accepts zero-value deposits can alter balances for other keys by letting zero or small deposits change behavior and thus violate this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any withdrawal amount, after calling CashOut(am) the balances mapping at the caller's address equals its prior balance minus am (i.e., CashOut never changes other accounts' balances); the mutant that accepts all deposits (including zero) can cause other accounts' balances to differ after CashOut, breaking this property for some inputs.

For any caller and any withdrawal amount, calling CashOut(amount) never changes balances of any OTHER address (only the caller's balance may decrease by amount); the mutant that indiscriminately accepts deposits (including zero) can cause balances of other addresses to change after CashOut for some inputs.

For any depositor A, if some other address B has balance 0 before A calls CashOut(x) (with x <= A's balance) then after the call B's balance in the contract remains 0; the mutant that accepts arbitrary (including zero) deposits can cause previously-zero balances of other addresses to become nonzero after a CashOut, so this rule is violated for some inputs.

Reference C: If an address B has zero balance before any sequence where some address A calls CashOut(v) (v <= A's balance), then B's balance remains zero after the CashOut; the mutant that accepts all deposits (including zero) can make previously-zero balances become nonzero for some inputs, so this invariant is broken by the mutant.
After calling Deposit with value X >= MinDeposit, c.balances(addr) increases by exactly X (i.e., balance_after - balance_before == X).

For any caller and amount, if Deposit is called with value strictly greater than the contract's MinDeposit then the caller's balance in C increases (is nonzero) afterwards.
Deposits with value strictly greater than MinDeposit do not leave the caller's recorded balance zero (i.e., such deposits must update balances[msg.sender] to a nonzero value).

Reference contract C always increases balances[msg.sender] when Deposit is called with msg.value >= MinDeposit; the mutant mistakenly skips that path for msg.value == MinDeposit (it only proceeds for msg.value > MinDeposit), so after CashOut the stored balances can differ for some fuzzed deposit amounts and actors.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit increases that caller's balances by the sent amount (so after depositing then cashing out some amount, the contract's balances mapping for that caller reflects the net change); the mutant wrongly treats msg.value == MinDeposit as too small and can leave balances unchanged causing balances to differ after CashOut for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor address a and deposit amount v >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit() increases C.balances(a) by v (so after depositing then CashOut of x<=balance, balances reflect net change); the mutant erroneously treats v==MinDeposit as too small (it returns) so for some fuzz inputs balances differ after CashOut.

For any depositor addr and deposit value v >= MinDeposit and any cashout amount x <= deposited balance, after performing Deposit(v) then CashOut(x) the contract's balances(addr) equals initial balance + v - x; the mutant incorrectly treats v == MinDeposit as too small and can leave balances unchanged, so balances differ for some fuzzed v equal to MinDeposit.

For any depositor and amounts, if a Deposit of value >= MinDeposit was made, then after a subsequent successful CashOut the mapping balances(someKey) reflects the net changes (initial + deposits - cashouts); the mutant returns early for msg.value == MinDeposit so some deposits of exactly MinDeposit never update balances and thus balances(...) can differ after CashOut for some fuzzed inputs.
